review_candidates.title: Associate Scientist - Single Cell Genomics Core / Neurocytometry Core
review_candidates.description: Location Memphis, TN Category Laboratory Sciences & Support Department Developmental Neurobiology Shift Weekday Day Position Type Full Time Scheduled Weekly Hours 40 Req # JR7066 Job Description The Associate Scientist position will have responsibilities in both the Single Cell Genomics Core and the Neurocytometry Core within the Department of Developmental Neurobiology at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. The candidate will independently perform tasks related to both cores - supporting single-cell sample processing, sequencing workflows, flow cytometry, instrument operation, user training, and multicolor panel design. The Single Cell Genomics and Neurocytometry Cores provide investigators studying the developing and diseased nervous system with access to single-cell genomic and flow cytometric technologies optimized for neural tissue. The Associate Scientist will support both cores, helping researchers isolate cells or nuclei and generate high-quality single-cell and flow cytometry datasets in support of developmental neurobiology, cancer, and translational research programs across the institution. This position combines hands-on operation, troubleshooting, and quality control of single-cell sequencing platforms (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium) with instrument setup, calibration, and multicolor panel design on flow cytometers and cell sorters. The successful candidate will work closely with core leadership and investigators across the Department of Developmental Neurobiology to optimize tissue dissociation protocols, complete library preparations, develop and run new high-parameter cytometry panels, and train users on both platforms. The Ideal Candidate Will Have The Following Strong background in developmental biology, molecular biology, neuroscience, stem cell biology, or a closely related field. Strong competence in designing, executing, and troubleshooting independent experiments using existing or newly developed protocols. Experience with single-cell genomic workflows (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium, single-cell RNA-seq library preparation) is preferred. Familiarity with neural tissue dissociation and analysis of neuronal, glial, and other cell populations in the brain and spinal cord. Hands-on experience with flow cytometry and cell sorting instrumentation, including instrument setup, calibration, and troubleshooting. Proficient knowledge of molecular biology and experience designing and analyzing multicolor/high parameter flow cytometry panels. Demonstrated experience with flow data analysis platforms (e.g., FlowJo, DIVA, OMIQ) and Microsoft Office products. Demonstrated success in training and supporting other technicians, students, and investigators. Strong organizational and communication skills Positive attitude with strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative, team-oriented approach. Interest in learning new technologies Job Responsibilities Independently perform experiments using existing, modified, or newly developed techniques/protocols. Accurately record experimental procedures and data Prepare and report results/ data leading to posters, presentations, or publications Set up protocols using new or modified laboratory techniques and troubleshoot experiments independently. Identify experimental data pertinent to the analysis problem; process, organize, and summarize data; report results. Independently perform single-cell sample processing, including neural tissue/cell dissociation, viability assessment, and loading onto single-cell sequencing platforms (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium). Coordinate sample intake, quality control, and sequencing run scheduling for the Single Cell Genomics Core and communicate results and troubleshooting steps to investigators. Establish, modify, and implement Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for routine maintenance and performance evaluation of flow cytometers and associated instrumentation. Independently perform instrument setup, sample acquisition, calibration, alignment, troubleshooting; oversee instrument repair and service coordination. Train technicians, students, and investigators on cytometry concepts, including instrument startup/shutdown, routine maintenance, sample acquisition, and basic data analysis. Collaborate with investigators to develop, evaluate, and optimize multicolor flow cytometry assays, including high-parameter panels. Perform regular cell sorting services and support users in developing technically sound, biologically relevant cytometry-based approaches. Provide ongoing support for monitoring, maintenance, ordering, and purchasing of equipment and supplies as needed. Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and the institution. Maintain regular and predictable attendance. Minimum Education And/or Training Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific area Minimum Experience 7 + years of research experience is required 5 + years of research experience is required with a Master's degree 2 + years of research experience is required with a PHD Experience leading and supporting research experiments preferred Some experience leading lab and scientific project coordination, maintenance, and other research support activities preferred Experience in guiding and training other laboratory personnel preferred Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role Compensation In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $65,520 - $114,400 per year for the role of Associate Scientist - Single Cell Genomics Core / Neurocytometry Core. review_candidates.title: Advanced Practice RN Provider-Life Flight
review_candidates.description: Location: METROHEALTH MEDICAL CENTER Biweekly Hours: 80.00 Shift: 8:00 AM TO 5:00 PM Where Critical Care Meets Flight Medicine Do you thrive in high-acuity environments where every clinical decision matters? Are you ready to practice at the highest level of advanced practice nursing while providing critical care in one of the most dynamic clinical environments? The Department of Emergency Medicine at The MetroHealth System , a nationally recognized academic medical center and principal teaching affiliate of Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine , is seeking an experienced Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP or ACNP) to join Metro Life Flight , one of Northeast Ohio’s premier critical care transport programs. This is an exceptional opportunity to provide advanced critical care aboard helicopter and ground critical care transport units. As part of a highly skilled multidisciplinary team of physicians, advanced practice providers, flight nurses, paramedics, pilots, and EMS professionals, you will care for critically ill and injured patients requiring rapid transport to specialized tertiary and quaternary care centers throughout the region. Why Metro Life Flight? Deliver advanced critical care during helicopter and ground transport. Practice with a high degree of autonomy while collaborating closely with Emergency Medicine physicians and multidisciplinary specialists. Care for complex trauma and critically ill medical, surgical, cardiac, neurologic, respiratory, and high-risk obstetrical patients. Utilize advanced critical care procedures, monitoring, medications, and technologies. Participate in education, simulation, quality improvement, and research initiatives. Practice in a unique environment that combines critical care medicine, emergency medicine, and flight medicine. What You’ll Do Assess, stabilize, and manage critically ill and injured adult and pediatric patients during transport. Develop and implement evidence-based treatment plans for complex, time-sensitive clinical conditions. Manage mechanical ventilation, invasive monitoring, vasoactive medications, blood products, and advanced cardiac and critical care therapies. Perform and/or assist with advanced critical care procedures within established scope of practice and program competencies. Collaborate with EMS agencies, trauma teams, intensivists, surgeons, specialty services, and referring and receiving hospitals. Provide comprehensive critical care throughout the transport continuum, from referring facility or scene through arrival at the receiving center. Promote safe transport operations, clinical excellence, and optimal patient outcomes. Contribute to ongoing education, simulation, quality improvement, and clinical research. Why You’ll Love Working Here Academic affiliation with Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine. Practice within a nationally recognized academic health system. Comprehensive onboarding, orientation, and ongoing professional development. Continuing education and opportunities to advance clinical expertise. Teaching and mentoring opportunities with residents, fellows, nurses, paramedics, and other learners. Strong physician and multidisciplinary collaboration. Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The opportunity to practice critical care medicine in a unique prehospital and transport environment. Qualifications Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) or higher. Graduate of an accredited Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) or Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (ACNP) program. Current Ohio RN and APRN licensure and national board certification. Current AHA BLS certification. Eligibility for clinical privileges through The MetroHealth System. Critical care, emergency medicine, trauma, or transport experience preferred. Demonstrated ability to function effectively in high-acuity, rapidly changing clinical environments. Strong communication, clinical judgment, and multidisciplinary collaboration skills. Join Our Mission At Metro Life Flight, every mission presents an opportunity to make a difference when time, expertise, and decisive clinical care matter most. If you are an experienced Acute Care Nurse Practitioner who is passionate about critical care, emergency medicine, and caring for patients in a uniquely challenging environment, we invite you to explore a career with Metro Life Flight . To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter to: Eloy Vázquez, Sr. Provider Recruiter The MetroHealth System Email: evazquez@metrohealth.org

review_candidates.title: University of Florida - Assistant Professor, History of the Indian Ocean World | H-Net
review_candidates.description: University of Florida - Assistant Professor, History of the Indian Ocean World Institution: University of Florida Institution Type: College / University Department: History Location: Florida, United States Position: Assistant Professor The Department of History at the University of Florida, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, is accepting applications for a full-time (1.0 FTE), nine-month, tenure-accruing appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor in the history of the Indian Ocean world beginning August 16, 2027. We invite applications from scholars of the Indian Ocean world, with an open chronological specialization and a focus on transregional dynamics – economic, migratory, legal, gender, environmental, social, cultural, and linguistic, among others. We are seeking a historian whose research is grounded in the histories, languages, and cultures of one or more specific region, i.e. South Asia, Southeast Asia, Eastern Africa, or the Middle East. At the same time, the candidate will be able to bridge regions of the Indian Ocean world and address teaching coverage needs in global history.In making this hire, the department seeks to build on and complement existing strengths in European empires and transoceanic and maritime history (of the Atlantic, Caribbean, and Gulf) while also enabling the study of global histories not defined by European imperial expansion. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching a diverse body of undergraduate and graduate students and maintain robust research and publication agenda commensurate with a top-tier research institution. Teaching responsibilities include introductory, upper-division, and graduate courses in Asian, African, or Middle East history as well as courses based on thematic approaches to world history and in the University’s Quest 1 program. The appointee will also contribute to the department’s graduate program through mentoring students, offering seminars, and chairing and serving on departmental and university committees, including those in other departments. The position offers opportunities to engage with the University of Florida Libraries’ extensive collections and to benefit from the support, resources, and activities of several interdisciplinary centers and programs including the the Center for African Studies, the Center for Medieval and Early Modern Studies, the Center for Latin American Studies, the Center for European Studies, the Bud Shorstein Center for Jewish Studies, the Department of Gender, Sexuality, and Women’s Studies, the Center for Arts, Migration and Entrepreneurship, and the Center for Humanities and the Public Sphere. Expected Salary The salary is competitive and commensurate with rank, qualifications and experience. review_candidates.title: Spuiter (Hoogeveen, 2 ploegendienst)
review_candidates.description: Wie zijn wij? Wil jij werken aan technische hoogstaande vliegtuigonderdelen en heb je hiervoor de juiste, technische achtergrond? Dan hebben we bij GKN Fokker Aerospace in Hoogeveen volop mogelijkheden voor jou. Voor GKN Fokker in Hoogeveen zoeken wij namelijk nog een ervaren onderdelenspuiter. GKN Fokker Aerospace is een erkende, eersteklas specialist in het ontwerp, de ontwikkeling en de fabricage van lichtgewicht constructies en modules voor de defensie- en civiele industrie. Wat doet een spuiter bij GKN Fokker Aerospace? Zelfstandig spuiten van vliegtuigonderdelen met diverse verschillende verfsystemen; Mengen van verven conform werkvoorschrift en juiste viscositeiten; Met behulp van een handspuitpistool aanbrengen van primer en meerdere aflaklagen in een spuitcabine; Beoordelen van je eigen werk, zoals: gesloten verflaag, laagdikte, glansgraad; Administratieve afhandeling zoals het digitaal invullen van spuitregistratie kaarten. Jouw profiel en competenties Vakdiploma in de richting van industrieel lakverwerker en/of schadeherstelspuiter; Enige ervaring als spuiter; Computervaardigheden; Kennis van de moderne Engelse taal; Kwaliteitsgericht, nauwkeurig en leergierig. Ons aanbod Een uitdagende, fulltime baan in een twee ploegendienst bij een organisatie met een rijke historie op het gebied van vliegtuigbouw. Daarnaast wordt er door GKN Aerospace geïnvesteerd in training en begeleiding van iedere nieuwe medewerker, waardoor je de kans krijgt je te ontwikkelen tot specialist. De medior schaal die bij deze functie hoort is schaal E van de cao metaal elektro. Afhankelijk van je opleiding en ervaring kun je ook ingeschaald worden in de junior- of senior schaal; Naast de basisvoorwaarden hebben wij ook goede secundaire voorwaarden, zoals 40 vakantiedagen. Solliciteren? Deze rol wordt vervuld via Randstad. Via de link kom je op hun pagina. Hier zie je alle vacatures staan en kan je direct solliciteren. Fokker vacatures | Werken bij Fokker | Randstad
